title: Staggered credits & milestone prompts to increase PLG upgrade conversion
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a multi-arm experiment to test whether staggered credit lifetimes combined with usage-based milestone prompts and an enterprise QA completion incentive increase PLG conversion and early retention without materially increasing credit cost. We will compare: (A) baseline one-off credit grant (control), (B) larger upfront credits with 30-day expiry, (C) smaller upfront credits + milestone-triggered micro-topups and contextual upgrade CTAs, and (D) variant that offers extended credits for enterprise prospects who complete a short security questionnaire and consent to contract outreach. Primary hypothesis: milestone nudges + micro-topups create more product-first engagement and lift paid conversion by 8-12% relative to control. Secondary hypothesis: enterprise QA incentive reduces sales friction for high-touch deals and increases MQL->SQL rate for larger ACV accounts.
acceptance_criteria: A statistically significant uplift in 30-day paid conversion for any treatment vs control (target lift >= 8%)
No more than 10% increase in gross credits consumed per new signup (cost cap)
Instrumentation emits milestone events (tokens_used, milestone_unlocked, micro_topup_granted, enterprise_qa_completed) and dashboards updated
Design and messaging reviewed and approved by Growth Design and Legal for the enterprise QA prompt
Playbook for follow-up by Sales/CS on enterprise QA completions created and shared
experiment_design: Control: existing free credits (e.g., $50 equivalent) single expiry 30 days, baseline onboarding flow
Arm B: larger one-time credit (+40%) with same expiry to test pure size effect

Arm C: baseline size but split into staggered amounts: initial + 2 micro-topups at token milestones (e.g., 500, 2500 tokens) with in-app contextual upgrade prompts tied to the feature the user used most

Arm D: same as Arm C + enterprise path: if user indicates company email domain and opts into 'enterprise evaluation', show 1-minute security questionnaire; on completion grant additional 14-day extended credits and route lead to enterprise sales queue
Randomize at account level for users with company-email vs consumer email and stratify by region to avoid region-specific bias
Duration: min 6 weeks or until 20k new accounts enrolled (whichever comes later), with interim check at 2 weeks for instrumentation
Primary metrics: 30-day paid conversion, 7/30-day retention (DAU/WAU for experiment cohort), credit consumption per converted user, MQL->SQL conversion for enterprise-path users
links: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1example - sample size calc and power analysis

rollout_plan: Week 0-1: Implement telemetry and gating flags (ENG). Design final copy and assets (DES). Legal signoff for enterprise wording.
Week 2: Internal QA, smoke tests, and soft-launch to 5% of new signups to validate events and spend caps
Week 3-7: Full experiment at target ramp to 100% of new signups until sample size hit (monitor daily for anomalies)
Post-experiment: 2-week analysis period, present results to GTM and execs, and decide on rollout strategy for winning variant
risks_mitigation: Risk: micro-topups could encourage wasteful consumption and increase credits costs. Mitigation: implement per-account credit spend cap and monitor cost delta daily
Risk: enterprise QA prompt may deter evaluation signups. Mitigation: make QA opt-in and only show to company emails; A/B test prompt copy
Risk: incorrect instrumentation. Mitigation: smoke tests, staging replay, and event-level assertions before ramp
Risk: legal/regulatory concerns for data collected in QA. Mitigation: minimal questionnaire, no PII storage, Legal sign-off required
